q: The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the _____
e: The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the torque. Do not trade torque for moment of inertia or angular momentum.
Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. Torque is a vector quantity. Do not trade vector for scalar or dimensionless.

q: The vector form of torque is expressed as _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The vector form of torque is expressed as boldsymbol{tau} = F × r. boldsymbol{tau} = F · r or boldsymbol{tau} = r · F is a different relation from boldsymbol{tau} = F × r.

q: The magnitude of torque is defined as the product of the force and the _____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The magnitude of torque is defined as the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum. Do not trade perpendicular distance for horizontal distance or angular distance.

q: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum is also called the _____
e: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum is also called the moment arm. Do not trade moment arm for lever arm or force arm.

q: In SI units, torque is measured in _____
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. In SI units, torque is measured in newton metre (N m). joule or kg m² s⁻² is a different relation from newton metre (N m).

q: If a force acts at an angle of $90^{\circ}$ to the lever arm, then the moment arm $d$ is equal to _____
e: If a force acts at an angle of 90° to the lever arm, then the moment arm d is equal to r. zero or r sin θ is a different relation from r.

q: The line along which a force is considered to act is called the _____
a: line of action of the force
e: The line along which a force is considered to act is called the line of action of the force. Axis of rotation or pivot line is not this quantity.

q: Examples of the turning effect of force include all of the following EXCEPT _____
a: tightening a nut with a spanner
e: Examples of the turning effect of force include all of the following EXCEPT dropping a ball vertically. Opening a door or tightening a nut with a spanner is not this quantity.

q: The point about which an object turns when a force is applied is known as the _____
e: The point about which an object turns when a force is applied is known as the fulcrum or pivot. Do not trade fulcrum or pivot for center of mass or axis of symmetry.
